blocks.text: 1. PR-AUC
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445338924-169596084.png

ROC-AUC, the previous topic, plotted True Positive Rate against False Positive Rate. PR-AUC is a closely related metric built from a genuinely different pair of axes, explored in full depth throughout this topic.

It works by plotting Precision against Recall, both already covered in their own topics, at every threshold, a genuinely direct parallel to ROC-AUC's own structure already covered in the previous topic.
2. The Class Imbalance Problem
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445338926-610633219.png

This connects back to the class imbalance caveat, already covered in ROC-AUC. ROC-AUC can genuinely look overly optimistic when negative examples vastly outnumber positive ones, already covered as a real limitation there.
PR-AUC exists specifically to address this exact genuine limitation, giving this entire topic its own clear motivation rooted directly in the previous topic's own acknowledged weakness.
3. The PR Curve Concept

The genuinely core idea behind the PR curve plots Precision against Recall at every possible threshold, both already covered in their own topics, mirroring the ROC curve's own structure covered previously.
This produces a single curve that genuinely captures the tradeoff between these two metrics across all thresholds, giving a genuinely complete picture rather than a single-threshold snapshot.

blocks.text: 4. Why False Positive Rate Can Be Problematic

blocks.alt: Why False Positive Rate Can Be Problematic
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445338926-438071463.png

This connects back to False Positive Rate, already covered in ROC-AUC. False Positive Rate divides by the count of all negative examples, a genuinely huge number when imbalanced datasets are involved.

Even many false positives barely move that ratio, hiding a genuinely real problem behind a deceptively small, reassuring-looking False Positive Rate value, exactly the imbalance problem already covered earlier in this topic.
5. Why Precision Genuinely Avoids This
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445338927-560411023.png

This connects back to Precision, already covered in its own topic. Precision divides by the count of predicted positives instead, a genuinely much smaller, more sensitive denominator than the one already covered in the previous section.

False positives genuinely move this ratio far more noticeably, since predicted positives are typically a genuinely far smaller group than all negative examples combined, making Precision genuinely more responsive to real mistakes.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This difference in denominators, already covered in this topic, is the genuinely core mathematical reason PR-AUC handles imbalanced datasets more honestly than ROC-AUC does.

blocks.text: 6. Defining PR-AUC
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445338927-948052651.png
This connects back to the PR curve, already covered in this topic. PR-AUC is the Area Under that Precision-Recall Curve, a single summary number condensing the entire curve into one comparable value.

Genuinely higher values indicate a genuinely better precision-recall tradeoff across thresholds, following the same intuitive, higher-is-better scale already covered as ROC-AUC's own interpretation in the previous topic.
7. A Genuinely Important Baseline Difference
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445338928-206053291.png

This connects back to ROC-AUC's own random-guessing baseline of 0.5, already covered. PR-AUC's own random-guessing baseline genuinely depends on the fraction of positive examples instead, not a fixed 0.5.

This is a genuinely important difference to keep in mind when interpreting a given PR-AUC score, since a PR-AUC of 0.3 might be genuinely excellent or genuinely poor depending entirely on how rare the positive class actually is.

blocks.text: 8. Choosing Between ROC-AUC And PR-AUC
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445338929-909909747.png

This connects back to both ROC-AUC and PR-AUC, already covered. With roughly balanced classes, ROC-AUC and PR-AUC often tell a genuinely similar story, since the imbalance problem already covered barely applies there.
With severely imbalanced classes, PR-AUC genuinely gives the more honest, trustworthy picture, exactly the motivation already covered as this entire topic's own reason for existing.
9. Recognizing When PR-AUC Is Genuinely The Right Metric
This connects back to severe class imbalance, already covered as ROC-AUC's own genuine limitation. PR-AUC's focus on Precision, already covered, directly avoids that limitation.

Fraud Detection or rare disease screening, common genuinely imbalanced real tasks, are direct cases where PR-AUC gives a genuinely more trustworthy read than ROC-AUC would on these tasks specifically.
10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates computing PR-AUC on a genuinely imbalanced dataset, contrasting it with ROC-AUC on the exact same predictions to illustrate the difference already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import average_precision_score, roc_auc_score

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
n_samples = 1000
n_positive = 50  # a genuinely severe class imbalance, only 5% positive

true_labels = np.zeros(n_samples)
true_labels[:n_positive] = 1
rng.shuffle(true_labels)

# Simulating a mediocre classifier's predicted probabilities
predicted_probabilities = true_labels * rng.uniform(0.4, 0.9, n_samples) + (1 - true_labels) * rng.uniform(0.0, 0.6, n_samples)

pr_auc = average_precision_score(true_labels, predicted_probabilities)
roc_auc = roc_auc_score(true_labels, predicted_probabilities)

print(f"ROC-AUC: {roc_auc:.3f}")
print(f"PR-AUC: {pr_auc:.3f}")
print(f"\nPositive class fraction (already covered as the PR-AUC baseline in this topic): {n_positive / n_samples:.3f}")
print("Notice PR-AUC reads meaningfully lower than ROC-AUC on this genuinely imbalanced dataset, exactly the difference already covered in this topic")

blocks.text: 11. Evaluation Metrics: Module Complete

items: PR-AUC plots Precision against Recall at every possible threshold, mirroring ROC-AUC's own structure.
It exists specifically to address ROC-AUC's own genuine weakness on severely imbalanced datasets.
Precision uses a smaller, more sensitive denominator than False Positive Rate, making it more responsive to real mistakes.
PR-AUC is the Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve, with higher values indicating a better tradeoff.
Its random-guessing baseline depends on the fraction of positive examples, unlike ROC-AUC's fixed 0.5.
With balanced classes, ROC-AUC and PR-AUC often agree; with severe imbalance, PR-AUC is more trustworthy.
It is especially valuable for tasks like Fraud Detection or rare disease screening.
